4                      UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                       
5                     NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA                     
6                                                                         
7    LIONEL ANTUNES,                  Case No.  24-cv-06737-TLT           

8              Plaintiff,             ORDER DISMISSING CASE FOR           
                                      LACK OF SERVICE OF PROCESS          
9          v.                         AND BECAUSE IT IS BARRED UNDER      
                                      THE FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS          
10                                     REFORM, RECOVERY AND                
                                      ENFORCEMENT ACT OF 1989             
11    FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE        (FIRREA)                            
     CORPORATION,                                                         
12                                     Re: Dkt. No. 6                      
               Defendant.                                                 
13                                                                         
14        Lionel Antunes, Self-Represented Plaintiff, filed a Complaint with the Court on September 
15   25, 2024.  ECF 1.  After the summons was issued, the Court ordered Plaintiff to file Proof of 
16   Service of Summons verifying that the Complaint was served on Defendant Federal Deposit 
17   Insurance Corporation prior to the expiration of the 90-day statutory requirement.  ECF 5.  To 
18   date, the Plaintiff has not demonstrated that Defendant was properly served1.  ECF 6. 
19        Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 4(c)(1), a summons must be served with a copy of 
20   the complaint.  The plaintiff is “responsible for having the summons and complaint served within 
21   the time allowed by Rule 4(m) and must furnish the necessary copies to the person who makes 
22   service.”  Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(c)(1).  Rule 4(m) states that if a defendant is not served within 90 days 
23   after the complaint is filed, the court must dismiss the action without prejudice against the 
24   defendant.  If the plaintiff shows good cause for the failure to serve defendant within 90 days, the 
25   court must extend the time for service for an appropriate period.  Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(m).  Plaintiff 
26   also cannot serve Defendant himself.  Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(c)(2).        
27                                                                         
1        In this case, there is no evidence that Defendant received a summons.  ECF 1, 6.  Instead, 
2   Plaintiff sent Defendant a Notice of Lawsuit and Request to Waive Service of a Summons.  
3   Notably, it explicitly stated that the correspondence was neither a summons nor an official notice 
4   from the court.  ECF 6.                                               
5        In the alternative, Plaintiff also provided tracking information.  Id.  The record does not 
6   reflect, however, that someone other than Plaintiff made the attempt to serve Defendant.  Absent 
7   good cause, the Plaintiff was given until December 30, 2024 to serve the Defendant.  See Fed. R. 
8   Civ. P. 4(m).  It appears that Plaintiff attempted to serve Defendant himself, never served a 
9   summons, and did not show good cause for the failure to serve within 90 days after the complaint 
10   was filed.  As such, Plaintiff failed to properly serve the Defendant. 
11        Arguably, if the Defendant were properly served, the Financial Institutions Reform, 
12   Recovery and Enforcement Act of 1989 (FIRREA) provides separate grounds to dismiss the case.  
13   Plaintiff was a named Plaintiff in a nearly identical case that was dismissed with prejudice after 
14   the court determined that the case was barred by the FIRREA.  Harrington v. FDIC, No. 23-cv-
15   06296-HSG, 2024 WL 23406990, at *4 (N.D. Cal. July 12, 2024).  Under the FIRREA, the FDIC 
16   has the power to act as a receiver of the failed bank by succeeding “all rights, titles, powers, and 
17   privileges of the insured depository institution.”  O’Melveny & Myers v. F.D.I.C., 512 U.S. 79, 86 
18   (1994).  As a receiver, the FDIC “steps into the shoes of the failed financial institution, assuming 
19   all the rights and obligations of the defunct bank.” Sharpe v. F.D.I.C., 126 F.3d 1147, 1152 (9th 
20   Cir. 1997) (internal citations omitted).  To allow the FDIC to perform its duties as a receiver 
21   “promptly and effectively,” the FIREAA provides that “no court may take any action, except at 
22   the request of the [FDIC] by regulation or order, to restrain or affect the exercise of powers or 
23   functions of the [FDIC] as a conservator or receiver.”  Hindes v. FDIC, 137 F.3d 148, 160 (3d Cir. 
24   1998); 12 U.S.C. § 1821(j).                                           
25        The Harrington court found that the FDIC acted in its capacity as receiver in a manner 
26   consistent with its powers or functions and found that the remedies Plaintiff sought would restrain 
27   or affect the exercise of powers or functions of the FDIC.  Harrington, 2024 WL 23406990, at *3.  
    1    a receiver for the defunct bank.  /d.  If the Court were to grant Plaintiff's requested declaratory 
    2  |}  relief to prohibit “the Defendant from engaging in any transfer, sale, liquidation, or other 
    3    disposition of Newport Group trust fund balances fully vested in Plaintiff's name,” it would 
    4  |}  restrain the exercise of the FDIC’s powers as a receiver.  12 U.S.C. § 1821().  Because Plaintiff 
    5  || requests relief that would restrain its receivership powers, Plaintiff's action is impermissible under 
    6  || 12U.S.C. § 1821G). 
    7          Accordingly, the Court DISMISSES the case for lack of service of process and because 
    8    the underlying case is barred by the FIRREA.  Because Plaintiff cannot overcome the FIRREA 
    9  || bar, the Court DISMISSES the case with prejudice. 
   10          This Order terminates the case.  The initial case management conference scheduled for 
   11    January 9, 2025 is vacated.  The clerk of the court is ordered to close the case. 
              IT IS SO ORDERED. 
5    13    Dated: January 7, 2025
